name: appmanager-lite
description: Self-hosted landing portal: a single home page with quick access to each team's applications, plus authentication, user and team management, and self-service application management with administrator approval.
generatedFrom: Hand-maintained from source; update alongside structural, API, config, or data-model changes.

architecture.summary: A FastAPI + SQLite backend exposes a JSON API under /api and also serves the built React single-page app. The frontend is a Vite-built SPA that uses relative URLs so one build runs at the site root or behind a subpath reverse proxy.
architecture.style: monorepo, single deployable (backend serves the frontend)
architecture.runtimeTopology: One uvicorn process serves /api and the SPA; SQLite is the datastore; an optional remote nginx is configured over SSH to publish local-alias applications.
architecture.auth: Argon2id password hashing, optional OIDC/OAuth2 and SAML 2.0 SSO, server-side sessions, HttpOnly + SameSite=Strict + Secure session cookie, and an X-CSRF-Token header on state-changing requests. Roles (admin, user) and team membership are enforced server-side.

components.description: FastAPI application: JSON API under /api, SQLite persistence, auth/sessions, audit log, reverse-proxy automation, and SPA hosting.

envVars.name: APP_BASE_DIR
envVars.purpose: Base directory for resolving relative data, frontend, and log paths.

envVars.name: APP_BASE_PREFIX
envVars.purpose: Optional subpath prefix (e.g. /home); only needed for strict reverse-proxy setups that require the app to emit its public subpath. The app otherwise works behind a proxy unchanged via relative paths.

envVars.name: APP_ENABLE_AUTH
envVars.purpose: Enable authentication and access control.

envVars.name: APP_DEV
envVars.purpose: Dev mode: enables interactive API docs and relaxes cookie security.

envVars.name: APP_SECURE_COOKIES
envVars.purpose: Set the Secure flag on the session cookie.

envVars.name: APP_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS
envVars.purpose: Session lifetime in seconds (12 hours).

envVars.name: APP_DATA_DIR
envVars.purpose: SQLite database and runtime data location.

envVars.name: APP_DB_PATH
envVars.purpose: SQLite database file path.

envVars.name: APP_FRONTEND_DIST

envVars.name: APP_LOG_DIR
envVars.purpose: Directory for the consolidated log file.

envVars.name: APP_LOG_FILE

envVars.name: APP_LOG_LEVEL
envVars.purpose: Log level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR).

envVars.name: APP_LOG_TO_FILE

envVars.name: APP_AUTH_MODE
envVars.purpose: Authentication mode: local, sso, or both.

envVars.name: APP_SSO_LOCAL_LOGIN_ENABLED
envVars.purpose: Legacy fallback for local username/password login when APP_AUTH_MODE is unset.

envVars.name: APP_SSO_AUTO_PROVISION
envVars.purpose: Create local users on first successful SSO sign-in.

envVars.name: APP_SSO_DEFAULT_ROLE

envVars.name: APP_SSO_EMAIL_DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST

api.auth: Session cookie set on login; access levels are anonymous, user (any signed-in account), and admin.
api.csrf: State-changing requests (POST/PATCH/DELETE) require an X-CSRF-Token header matching the session token when auth is enabled.
api.docs: Interactive docs at /docs and the schema at /openapi.json are exposed only when APP_DEV is enabled.

routes.summary: Liveness check.
Current session and branding (works before authentication).
Read enabled SSO login providers for the login page.
Nginx auth_request endpoint for protecting reverse-proxied aliases.
Authenticate and start a session.
Start OIDC authorization-code login.
Handle OIDC provider callback and start a local session.
Start SAML service-provider initiated login.
Handle SAML assertion consumer service callback and start a local session.
Expose SAML service-provider metadata.
End the current session.
Change the signed-in user's own password.
Set the signed-in user's own UI theme (self-only; validated to the four theme ids; empty resets to the deployment default).
The signed-in user's SSH public key, derived user-id, and generation time (never the private key).
Download the signed-in user's own SSH key; requires part=private|public. Private downloads are audited (metadata only).

Replace the signed-in user's SSH keypair and rotate it on their servers (remove old public key, install new), and on the jump server using the account for the configured jump account model (the shared jumper account in shared mode, the user's own account otherwise); returns a per-server summary (audited, no key material).
Aggregate authenticated portal-launch and favorite statistics over a bounded date range.
Derived account-ID activity and favorite detail for one application statistics row.
Record an authenticated portal launch for a visible approved application.
List teams (name, order, icon) for any signed-in user.
List users.
Create a user (returns a generated password and per-template auto-provisioning results).
Update a user's role, teams, active state, or flags.
Reset a user's password (returns a generated password).
Delete a user.
List applications visible to the caller (optional team filter).
List applications the caller created.
List every application with creator and status.
Read the deployed nginx alias config for an application the caller can manage.
Create/submit an application (approval depends on role/self-service).
Update an application; admins also approve/reject here.
Delete an application (removes its nginx alias when applicable).
Query audit-log entries (optional category filter).
Read reverse-proxy configuration.
Update reverse-proxy configuration.
Read branding settings.
Update branding (app name, logo, collaborators, default theme, configured flag).
List teams (admin view).
Create a team.
Rename a team and/or change its icon.
Delete a team.
Set the sidebar order of all teams.
Read LXC/VM provider and provisioning-policy settings (the Proxmox API key is never returned; only a presence flag).

Update provider/policy settings (incl. selected Proxmox realms, user-pool prefix, and the add-to-pool toggle); touching provider connection fields runs a Proxmox connection test and stores its status and log.
Live template/VM list from the provider, honoring the name filter and templates-only toggle.
Live Proxmox authentication realms (GET /access/domains) for the admin realm multi-select; empty list when the provider is unconfigured or unreachable.
Onboard every active user to the configured jump server (idempotent); returns a per-user summary.
Switch the jump account model (per_user/shared); requires acknowledgment, re-syncs all users, and reverts on any failure.
List registered SSH keys (registry; no private material returned).
Register an SSH key: a key file path (kind=path) or a pasted private key stored encrypted (kind=stored, write-only).
Edit a registered SSH key (name, path, kind switch, or replace the stored key; allowed while referenced).
Delete a registered SSH key (409 if still referenced).
List registered server templates.
Register a server template (vmid, name, lxc|vm, registry admin key, optional main OS user, sudo and trusted-access flags).
Update a server template (incl. main user, sudo, trusted access).
Delete a server template.
Clone a bundle template (incl. a built-in) into a new editable, non-built-in template.
Enable or disable a bundle template; disabled templates are hidden from account downloads.
User-facing server-template options (id, name, kind only).

Whether the caller may create servers for their own account (with a reason when not) and whether they may edit their own servers' resources (allow_resource_edit: true for admins and any self-service user; no separate policy opt-in).
List enabled bundle templates (id, name, description) available to the signed-in user for download.

Download the rendered bundle as a zip (SSH config, private/public key without an extension, and a connect_server_<name>.sh script per server); the filename carries a UTC -YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS timestamp suffix. Contains the private key, so it is audited and never cached.
All servers the caller may see, grouped by owner, for the Servers section. Administrators see every user's servers (with destroy-failure detail); a non-admin sees only their own.

List a user's servers. Also runs the lazy deferred-deletion sweep (bounded, single-flight) and lazily backfills missing (0) CPU/memory/disk specs from the provider for guests with a vmid (bounded per request, persisted, fully guarded). Admins see servers whose destroy failed (with the error); owners do not.
Per-user provisioning usage vs. limits (servers, CPUs, memory, disk) for the create-form quota bars; administrators are reported as unlimited.

Historical CPU/memory/disk/network usage for a server over a timeframe (hour/day/week), read from Proxmox rrddata; returns available=false with a reason when there is no guest, the provider is unconfigured, or the read fails.

Create a server from a template: the request supplies only a name suffix and the full name is composed as '<template-slug>-<owner-id>-<suffix>' (globally unique, max 63 chars); clone (full), start + IP discovery for LXC (the container's real in-guest IP is read over SSH and recorded when the hypervisor corroborates it, else the hypervisor IP is kept), optional SSH public-key installation; VMs are cloned only and get a manual IP. Quotas apply to non-admin creators.

Set a VM's IP address manually, or change resources: LXC supports CPU/memory/grow-only disk, VM supports CPU/memory only (disk rejected); any self-service owner may change their own non-admin-managed server within quota, admins always (exempting the server from quotas). The response's reboot_required is a transient flag set after a VM CPU/memory change.

Reboot a running LXC or VM server; allowed for the self-service owner (even if admin-managed) or an admin. Rejects servers that failed provisioning, have a deletion pending/failed, or were never actually provisioned (no vmid/node).
Schedule deferred deletion: the server enters a 24-hour grace period, then a sweep stops and destroys the LXC/VM and removes the record (idempotent if already pending).
Cancel a pending deferred deletion before the grace window elapses.
Administrator-only: remove the server record even if its automatic destroy failed (a best-effort destroy is attempted first; the admin verifies the guest in Proxmox).

dataModel.migrations: Schema created via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; later columns added by additive, idempotent ALTER guarded by PRAGMA table_info. No version table.

tables.name: users
tables.description: Accounts with role, status, self-service flag, per-user apps server/port, and a per-user Ed25519 SSH keypair (generated at creation, backfilled by migration; key material is served only to the owning user).

tables.name: teams
tables.description: Administrator-managed teams with sidebar order and optional icon.

tables.name: sessions
tables.description: Server-side sessions with CSRF token and expiry.

tables.name: sso_auth_flows
tables.description: Short-lived OIDC/SAML state, nonce, and safe return path values used to validate SSO callbacks.

tables.name: applications
tables.description: Application entries with URL/alias, approval state, owner, alias upstream settings, per-alias auth, staged changes, and last reverse-proxy push result.

tables.name: audit_log
tables.description: Audit trail of actions, grouped by category (application, user, system). User-category server actions include server_create, server_update, server_reboot, server_delete/cancel, server_mesh (trusted SSH mesh outcome), and server_pool_add (Proxmox user-pool assignment outcome: ok/failed with the pool id).

tables.name: settings
tables.description: Single pinned row (id = 1) for reverse-proxy, branding, LXC/VM provider (Proxmox; API key stored write-only), and server-provisioning policy configuration. proxmox_realms (JSON list) and proxmox_pool_prefix drive the Proxmox user-pool assignment; provisioning_add_to_pool (default on) enables adding each created guest to its owner's pool. provisioning_allow_resource_edit is retained read/write for backward compatibility but no longer consulted for authorization (any self-service user may edit their own non-admin-managed server's resources) and is no longer surfaced in the admin UI.

tables.name: ssh_keys
tables.description: Registry of SSH keys usable across the app: a key file path (kind=path) or a private key stored encrypted at rest (kind=stored). Secret material is never returned by the API.

tables.name: server_templates
tables.description: Admin-registered Proxmox templates (LXC or VM) offered when creating user servers; admin key referenced from the ssh_keys registry. main_os_user is the single template-controlled account that receives the managed SSH key; when enable_sudo is on, provisioning atomically reasserts and verifies its AppManager-owned NOPASSWD sudoers drop-in. is_apps_server marks a template whose name is offered at user creation (a reference, resolved to a live server's host at alias-push time) and whose cloned servers are offered by name in application management's apps-server dropdown.

tables.name: user_servers
tables.description: Per-user provisioned or referenced LXC/VM servers with resource accounting and a secret-free creation transcript. admin_modified marks a server whose size was set by an administrator (admin resource edits are not quota-gated); it no longer prevents the self-service owner from resizing their own server (issue_023 -- quota still applies to the owner). Supports deferred deletion: deletion_requested_at marks a pending deletion (24-hour grace before the guest is destroyed) and deletion_error records a destroy failure (admin-only recovery). The API's is_apps_server flag is derived live from template_id's server_templates.is_apps_server (a deleted template yields false, never stale). The API's poolid is a response-only hint resolved live from Proxmox (a single cluster-wide lookup per list, best-effort) and never persisted; the server card shows it as a Pool badge. Trusted-access servers form one owner-scoped cross-account mesh: each server's template main account trusts every peer server's template main account. Established means every directed connection verifies; recoverable unverified results are retried. Reset access verifies the current bundle keypair, reasserts it on eligible template accounts and the configured jump account, then reconciles mesh and managed sudo; immutable user-ID markers preserve unmanaged jump keys (see server_mesh and server_access_reset audits).

tables.name: bundle_templates
tables.description: Downloadable user configuration bundles with field mappings. Built-in templates (is_builtin) render dynamically and cannot be edited/deleted (only cloned); disabled templates are hidden from account downloads.

directories.purpose: FastAPI application package (routers, data access, schemas, auth).
React + TypeScript source (components, lib, API client, types).
Static assets: fallback logo and the logo/team-icon catalogues.

conventions.testing: Backend: pytest (backend/tests). Frontend: vitest + Testing Library (*.test.ts[x]).
conventions.commits: Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, chore:, refactor:, ...).
conventions.branching: Feature branches with pull requests against main.
notes: All API queries use bound parameters; no SQL is built from user input.
Secrets (passwords, hashes, session ids, CSRF tokens) are never logged or audited.
Teams are administrator-managed; a clean install starts with no teams and no applications.
A single frontend build runs at the site root or behind a subpath via an injected <base href>.
